caption:
Mr Turtle spends all day behind the chair with his arms up, head tilted and hands gripping. Hairdressers and barbers load the neck, shoulders and forearms a lot, especially in a busy week.

A few things can help: pump the chair so you're working around chest height, step around the client rather than reaching, and take 30 seconds between appointments to drop your arms, roll your shoulders and shake out your hands. Remedial massage can ease tight shoulders and forearms, and it works well alongside those habits.

Numb or tingly fingers, hand weakness or pain that keeps building is worth a physio assessment. Book online via the link in bio ✂️
